The red exterior of the store is impressive. It's a bit far from the station, but if you take the bus, you can get off nearby.

Espresso served not in a German or Japanese cup, but in a cup made by a Korean ceramic artist (Song Min-ho)
I was surprised by the roasting point that overshadowed my likes and dislikes with flavors like lime and grapefruit.

The ribs of the glass were thin so the colorful notes could be fully felt.
It's like a roastery where you roast yourself with Easyster 1.8.
From 84mm flat burr grinder to Scodi 2 and Major V grinder

The espresso made with Cime CO05 retains its natural sweetness even though sugar has been removed, and its light smokiness and sticky texture are amazing.

The vivid silicone tea coaster with the right point awakens our brain, which often feels the bitter taste of coffee in a white cup.

I'm also curious about the brewed coffee brewed with the ek43s grinder and the very pretty Brewsta Pot.
This is a new espresso restaurant where you can enjoy luxury for just 3,500 won!

reviews.text: The most unique Korean dessert, walnut snacks. It contains plenty of healthy red bean paste that does not use sugar, making it perfect as a hearty bread or meal. As the name of the store suggests, these are authentic walnut snacks. A store where everything is handcrafted one by one by a warm store owner where you can feel the ‘affection’ of Korea. Coffee and other beverages can also be purchased. I stopped by to see the beautiful night view of Dongdaemun (Heunginjimun) and the beautiful Naksan Fortress Wall Road. It is a cozy store in a local village that is loved by many local residents, but the taste of the walnut snacks is truly like that of a small giant.

It's a small mortgage walnut snack shop in an alley that you can easily miss if you don't come looking for it. The owner is really friendly, and the English menu is well prepared, so it's not difficult for foreigners to order.

Walnut snacks are low in sugar, so they are easy to eat, and since they are freshly baked, they are warm and savory. It's not just a sweet snack, but it's light and still has the flavor of the ingredients, so I think it'll be a good fit for those who are trying Korean snacks for the first time!

Recommended if you want to experience a small but sincere Korean snack restaurant found in a local alley.

reviews.author: NU1T
reviews.text:
Compared to the espresso bars known these days, there aren't many espresso menus, so I was a little anxious and decided to try the espresso first, but after taking a sip, I immediately changed to set A and drank the strappazzato as well.

The espresso is delicious, and even though it rained that day, sitting at an outside table gave off a proper turn-of-the-century feel (resident of Dongsung-dong in the 80s and 90s). The interior structure is also unique.

In my experience, good coffee places have one thing in common: the baristas are humble and friendly, and this place is just like that.
Espresso bars are mushrooming these days, but it's hard to find the right place. It's been a while since I came to Daehak and found a good place and it's nice to donate.

I went to a cafe and asked if I could sit outside and eat because there were no seats inside, but the staff just said, “We’re very busy with orders.” My girlfriend and I were so dumbfounded that we asked if she would come back in 10-15 minutes. Then they just said that they were backordered again. So I just left and went back 30 minutes later. We stood in front of the counter to pack the cake, but the employee didn't come out of the kitchen, and when he did, he didn't even look at us, so he just picked up the cake from the shelf and went back into the kitchen. I don't know what "backlogged orders" has to do with anything. All you have to do is let them know that you have a backlog of orders. Plus, the cake didn't look that delicious from the beginning.

After tasting Korean vegetable bibimbap and Korean sausage sundae, it's a good place to take a break and have a cup of coffee at a cozy Starbucks overlooking the beautiful market. Starbucks has a nice atmosphere and is spacious, so there are many places to sit and a large window overlooking Gwangjang Market. The atmosphere of various concepts is beautiful. Twist. The snacks that can only be eaten at the Starbucks branch in Gwangjang Market, where you can feel the Korean tradition, such as the thread cake, and the interior are cool.

reviews.author: Yeon Woo Kim
reviews.text: This is a Starbucks store located in Seoul Gwangjang Market. It is located in the middle of a traditional market, so the surrounding atmosphere is lively and it is always crowded with tourists and locals. Although the entrance is relatively narrow, the interior is long and has a variety of seats. From the window seat, you can look down on the streets of Gwangjang Market, and it is also good for people-watching. The first floor is centered on ordering and pickup, and the second floor consists of a seating area. Although the spacing between seats is narrow, there are electrical outlets throughout, so using a laptop is not inconvenient. There is no separate parking space, and you must use a nearby paid parking lot. The staff is friendly and responds quickly even when there is a high volume of orders. This is a great store to have a cup of coffee before or after visiting the market.

reviews.text: It's been a while since I've been to Gwangjang Market, but it seems to have become a very young place and a lot of foreigners are enjoying it. Among them, Onion Gwangjang Market is a place where you can enjoy drinks and pastry pizza along the Cheonggyecheon Stream. It's amazing to see older people hanging out together and eating delicious coffee and bread, and it's somewhat unfamiliar to see people standing on the street eating pastries. The pastry tasted just as I expected, and the homemade strawberry jam was delicious. Personally, it was bland and the signature hazelnut latte was sour. Vintage goods are also on sale.

A bar-type coffee shop at the entrance of Gwangjang Market,

reviews.author: Hojoong Yi
reviews.text:
A makgeolli restaurant with delicious snacks. The food tastes so good that I want to visit again because I'm curious about the other snacks. It is good value for money, but the taste is far better than the price.

Oyster gratin is a dish that even people who are not good at eating oysters can eat without burden, as the fishy taste of oysters is taken out by the seasoned vegetables.

The soybean paste stir-fry dish feels somewhere between Mexican and Chinese food, but if you put it on a tortilla and eat it with sour sauce, it becomes a taco with a harmonious taste. The sour sauce is especially delicious. If you don't eat it wrapped in a tortilla, it may feel a little salty.

The highlight is adding noodles to the soybean paste dish. The noodles are like pasta noodles, but should they be called Yakisoba or Pasta? A wonderful plate is served. The addition of butter maximizes the richness.

I missed talking about makgeolli because I was only talking about the food, but the unique advantage of this restaurant is that you can try a variety of makgeolli. There may be differences in taste when it comes to makgeolli, but overall, it doesn’t feel like homemade makgeolli. The deep flavor is slightly lacking, and the sweet makgeolli leaves something to be desired.

The snacks were menu items that would be found in many bars in Euljiro, and the makgeolli lineup was varied, which was nice. The makgeolli (not applicable) made at this house is especially delicious, so be sure to try it!

It boasts a punchy volume and output so strong that the vibration can be felt even outside the store.

What did El Condorpasar do wrong to hate him so much? It was a bit sad.

reviews.author: Beom Big
reviews.text:
The first visit was on June 25th, probably around 8:40 to 9:00 PM. I found out by chance, and while looking at the grocery store below, I came up and sat down for a while. I decided to visit again next time, apologized, and on my way out, I asked for corkage for a future visit. The female employee informed us that ‘if you order one bottle, you can bring one bottle to drink.’ There was no separate information about corkage charge.

And on July 9th, I visited again with friends who had come to Seoul from the provinces. Likewise, I was told that separate reservations cannot be made after 8pm, so they said they would contact me and they would guide me, but I couldn't get in touch with them even after calling more than 3 times, so I just left. Fortunately, there was a rooftop (outdoor) seat, and while I was sitting down, I asked the staff, ‘We’re going to order a bottle, can we drink the wine we brought with corkage?’ and was told, “You know, that’s right.” There was no information about the charge on the menu or at the reception, so I only found out when I made the payment. There is a corkage fee. I am leaving a review because I am unclear as to whether it is a problem with the guidance and service or whether it is my fault for not finding out that there is a corkage fee of course.

When I first inquired, they did not tell me that I could get one bottle per order and how much it would cost, but I did not look at the menu very closely. Since I only visited once, there wouldn't have been any misunderstanding if they had informed me that there would be a fee just for sitting, but it's a pity. It was a meeting with acquaintances after a long time, and I was about to leave in good spirits, but then I received an unexpected announcement. The reason I didn't tell them right away was that I had been drinking, so I came back in case the conversation got emotional. Of course, they said they had not received any information about the charge and only checked availability, so they repeated the usual instructions. The response is disappointing. I thought it was a nice space and an attractive location, but the ending was unsatisfactory, so I keep feeling sad in many ways.

To add a little more, I agree that the corkage policy is at the discretion of the business and the business owner's choice. Therefore, I believe that customers have the right to be provided with accurate information and that the response in that regard should be done without misunderstanding. Misunderstandings from the user's perspective are common, and it may be a bit difficult to say that this is common, but if we look at a few cases first, a corkage fee is charged but there is a limit on the number of bottles, or there is no limit on the number of bottles. If you have to choose only the wine in the business and corkage is not possible, corkage is possible but there is no corkage fee, I think this is the case. However, if you have to order a bottle of wine from the business and there is a cost involved, if that is also a general case, you should provide separate guidance so that you can receive information without misunderstanding and take it into consideration when choosing a location.

On the evening of June 25th, if I had not been notified at that time, I would be cautious, but I would have had to order a bottle within the establishment, and if there was a separate charge, I would have considered other places, and I would not have chosen the corkage wine. That's it.
